solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Budget holiday planning at any cost must include Italy

indicators.note: must include says the rearranged letters wrap round the next piece
planning suggests the letters of the following phrase are being worked out and arranged anew

parts.note: I is the international vehicle registration code for Italy

explanation.surface: Someone working out a cheap holiday finds Italy must feature whatever the price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planning' rearranges AT ANY COST into STAYCATON, and 'must include' puts I inside it, between T and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday spent at home rather than abroad is the classic cheap break, a budget getaway.

clue.text: Location making sense in audition

indicators.note: in audition means as heard by a listener, so the word for sense is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: A place that makes sense when an actor tries out for a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in audition' turns SIGHT into the same-sounding spelling SITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a place or position, a straightforward synonym for location.

clue.text: One can under pressure!

parts.note: a spray can holds its contents under pressure, so it is literally one can that is pressurised

explanation.surface: A rallying cry that anybody can cope when the heat is on.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'can' as a verb, as in 'one is able to'; it is really the noun, a canister of pressurised spray.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray canister keeps its contents compressed, so it is a container kept under pressure.

clue.text: Resist charges for designing machines in store

indicators.note: designing suggests the letters of the preceding words are reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Shoppers opposing price rises for some new shop equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for designing' rearranges the thirteen letters of RESIST CHARGES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tills that record sales and hold cash are the machines found at a shop's checkout.

clue.text: Fresher-smelling South African city

parts.note: something with a sharper, more pungent scent is tangier

explanation.surface: A South African city with a cleaner, fresher smell.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pulls 'South African' together; split it, so that 'South' gives S and 'African city' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangiers is the older English spelling of Tangier, the Moroccan port city in North Africa.

clue.text: Love to put a value on talk

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O
to rate something is to value or assess it

explanation.surface: Love is impossible to price, says someone in conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak at length, usually pompously, so it is a kind of talking.

clue.text: Tea, say, with small Scottish dainty

indicators.note: say signals that the word is heard rather than written, so we keep its sound as a letter

parts.note: the drink tea is pronounced like the letter T
wee is a Scots word for small

explanation.surface: A small Scottish cup of tea served daintily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you that Tea gives the letter T, since they sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee means excessively quaint or dainty, sweetly pretty to the point of affectation.

clue.text: New law from producing metal

indicators.note: new signals that the following letters are made into something fresh, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A fresh piece of legislation leads to a metal being produced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges LAW FROM; 'producing' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfram is the alternative name for tungsten, the chemical element with symbol W.

clue.text: Simple carbon, for example, used on a railway

indicators.note: in a down clue, used on means the first piece sits on top of the next one

parts.note: carbon is one example of a chemical element
taken as written

explanation.surface: Carbon being used as fuel on a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for example' marks carbon as an instance, so it gives the class word ELEMENT, not C.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary means basic or straightforward, as in an elementary question, so it is a synonym of simple.

clue.text: Go with lad for thrills

parts.note: a go in a game is a turn
a lad can be a son, a male child

explanation.surface: A parent hands the controller to the boy so he can have fun.
explanation.definitionFit: If something turns you on it excites or thrills you, an idiomatic phrasal verb.

clue.text: Let off the hook, sailors love getting drunk

parts.note: ABs are able seamen, ordinary sailors

indicators.note: drunk suggests something unsteady and jumbled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Sailors falling for each other while drunk escape punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting drunk' rearranges ABS plus LOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve is to free someone from blame or obligation, the same idea as releasing them from a difficulty.

clue.text: What children may have to wear for lunch, if room so untidy

definitions.text: What children may have to wear

indicators.note: untidy suggests a jumble, so the preceding letters are messed into a new order

explanation.surface: Children's clothes thrown about the room while they eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidy' rearranges the letters of LUNCH IF ROOM SO; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Many schools require pupils to wear set clothing, the outfit children must put on each day.

clue.text: Addition to bill from mass accusation?

parts.note: Mass is a church service
an accusation is a criminal charge

explanation.surface: A restaurant adds an extra fee after a church accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Restaurants often add a fixed percentage for the staff on top of the meal's cost, a surcharge to the check.

clue.text: Convenient-sounding ship's activity requiring skill

indicators.note: sounding says the word for convenient is spelt as it is heard, not as written

parts.note: handy means convenient
a craft is a vessel, a ship

explanation.surface: Building a model ship is a handy skill to have.
explanation.walkthrough: '-sounding' turns HANDY into HANDI, which sounds the same; the 's of ship's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Handicraft is skilled work with the hands, such as pottery or weaving.

clue.text: Symbolic tale making you really upset about travel

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters wrap round the next piece
upset suggests the word is knocked over and jumbled, a rearrangement

parts.note: to travel is to go

explanation.surface: A fable whose violence makes you very distressed about a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' makes ALLERY, which 'about' wraps round the travel word; 'making you' only links definition to wordplay, though it reads as part of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegory is a story in which characters and events stand for abstract ideas.

clue.text: Arrangement by which mother is protected by garrison

indicators.note: being protected by something means being enclosed within it

parts.note: a garrison is a fort
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother sheltered by the troops, in some arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A format is the layout or arrangement of something, such as a page or a show.

clue.text: Affable student welcomed by country worker once

indicators.note: being welcomed by someone means being taken inside

parts.note: a peasant was a farm labourer of old times
L is for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A friendly learner greeted by a farmhand of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomed by' puts L inside PEASANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasant means agreeable and friendly in manner, close in sense to affable.

clue.text: Material to give daughter a disguise

parts.note: taken as written
a mask hides the face, a disguise

explanation.surface: Giving a girl a mask for a fancy dress party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to give' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a rich woven fabric with a pattern visible on both sides.

clue.text: Brute's in form — on steroids!

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A thug is in peak shape thanks to performance drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Brute's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A monster is a cruel or hideous person, a savage, much like a brute.

clue.text: Fish left in sink

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a ship that founders sinks

explanation.surface: A fish left in the kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sink' looks like the kitchen fitting, but it is the verb, as when a ship goes down.
explanation.definitionFit: A flounder is a flatfish, an example of a fish.

clue.text: Surgeon has time in study first

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a den is a private room for study
first is written 1ST, read as IST

explanation.surface: A surgeon spends time studying before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives IST, from 1ST with the 1 read as I; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dental surgeon is the formal title for a person who treats teeth.

clue.text: Attention paid in Mass

definitions.meaning: close attention to a task is focused mental effort
a mass of people or things is a dense gathering, a heavy clustering in one place

explanation.surface: Worshippers paying close attention during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like the church service, but it means a dense gathering; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Concentration means both focused mental effort and the clustering of things densely together.

clue.text: Touch that's integral to getting even

indicators.note: integral to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small bit of revenge is part of getting even.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace or hint of something, a touch.

clue.text: Person who does clean fish

definitions.meaning: a cleaning lady, a charwoman, who does housework

explanation.surface: A cleaner who prepares fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Char is both British slang for a cleaning woman and the name of a fish related to trout.

clue.text: Craftsman pictures tax-free investment (new)

parts.note: pictures are works of art
an ISA is a British individual savings account, a tax-free investment

explanation.surface: An artisan invests in new paintings using a tax-free savings account.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a UK tax-free savings account.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker, someone who makes things by hand.

clue.text: Get rid of boils spreading in a hospital

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: spreading suggests the letters are spread out and rearranged

explanation.surface: A hospital tries to get rid of boils that are spreading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' rearranges BOILS into OLIS, which goes inside A and H.
explanation.definitionFit: To abolish is to formally do away with something, like a law or custom.

clue.text: Thanks the Navy for a feature of the Lake District

definitions.text: a feature of the Lake District

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Thanking the Navy for a Lake District feature.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lake District is a mountainous region of northwest England; a tarn is a small mountain lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarn is a small mountain lake, characteristic of the English Lake District.

clue.text: Writer met rate for changing a line of verse

parts.note: a pen is a writer, the instrument that writes

indicators.note: changing suggests the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A poet finds a paid rate for changing a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for changing' rearranges MET RATE into TAMETER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentameter is a line of verse with five metrical feet.
